about: 1stcontact's backend settings (BUG-67). The project half of the seam
lagrange-framework BUG-49 opened: which model the builder's consultant runs
on, and how much room one reply gets, are decisions this repository makes.
WHY THE FILE EXISTS AT ALL. These were framework constants. When REQ-146
moved the model to claude-sonnet-5 and the ceiling from 4096 to 32000, this
project's route to those values was a framework release — it constructed the
backend naming neither, so the framework's opinion was the only thing on the
wire. BUG-49 made them configuration; this file is 1c exercising that, so
changing either is an edit here and nothing else.
The keys are the framework's schema, not ours: a backend it does not declare,
or a key that backend does not have, is rejected at start-up by
`configureBackends` naming the offending key. Settings merge per key over the
shipped defaults, so naming one value changes one thing.
max_tokens is 64000 because the builder's smallest legitimate page write is a
whole page. It is an ENFORCED ceiling the model cannot see — it does not
produce a shorter reply, it cuts the stream wherever it happens to be, and in
a tool call that yields broken JSON arguments rather than a smaller edit.
That is the failure BUG-67 was filed for: twelve consecutive `set_l1` calls
arriving with an empty input object at the 4096 cap. Anthropic's documented
default for STREAMING requests is ~64000 — the reason to go lower (~16000) is
HTTP timeouts on non-streaming requests, and the adapter passes stream: true,
so that reason does not apply here. Billing is per token actually generated,
so a high cap costs nothing until it is used; per-session spend is the right
cost control and this is not it.
claude-opus-5 has a 1M context window and a 128K output ceiling, so 64000 is
about half of what one reply may be and ~6% of the room the turn has — it does
not meaningfully compete with input. On Opus 5 thinking is ON by default and
max_tokens bounds thinking and response text TOGETHER, so this is a shared
budget rather than 64000 of reply — an argument for the ceiling being roomy,
which it is.
The adapter sends model, max_tokens, system, messages, tools and stream only.
That matters for this model: Opus 5 removes budget_tokens, temperature, top_p
and top_k, and refuses an assistant prefill, so a request carrying any of them
would 400. There is nothing here for it to refuse.
`claude_builder` IS A SECOND VARIANT OF THE SAME ADAPTER ([[REQ-295]]), not a
second provider. The framework's name list is open precisely for this — a host
running its delegated sessions on a cheaper model registers a variant and
configures that name's model here — and `ClaudeAPIBackend` reads its settings
under the name it was CONSTRUCTED with while reading the shipped floor under
the `claude` family. So this entry alone decides what a worker runs on, and
nothing about the line above it moves: the consultant keeps opus-5 and its
64000, because a delegation that quietly changed the caller's model would be
the one change this whole lever must not make.
32000 rather than 64000, and the asymmetry is deliberate. The ceiling exists
because the consultant's smallest legitimate write is a whole page and Opus 5
shares max_tokens between thinking and reply. A worker writes pages too, so it
needs real room — but it is doing bounded, named pieces of work rather than
holding a whole engagement, and a ceiling is the one bound a delegation has on
a single turn. Billing is per token actually generated, so this costs nothing
until it is used.
`claude_coordinator` IS THE GROUP CHAT'S SECOND MEMBER ([[REQ-357]]), a third
variant of the same adapter and deliberately not `claude_builder`: the
coordinator converses in the room and reads, it never builds, so what it runs on
is a separate decision from what a worker runs on and each is one edit here.
Haiku, for DOC-62's latency reason — a one-second participant beside a
ten-minute one. 16000 because it writes contributions, not pages.
THE CONSULTANT IS ON claude-opus-5-5 ([[REQ-362]]): the current Opus, and
cheaper than opus-5 on every counter — most of all on cache reads, which are
the consultant's biggest line. Same 1M window and 128K output ceiling, so
64000 stands for the reasons above. `context_window` is declared because the
installed framework's model table does not yet name opus-5-5 — the one case
that key exists for, and `checkProjectWindows` would refuse to start without
it. Delete it once the framework's table carries the model, so the window
follows the next change of `model` rather than outliving it.
OPUS 5.5 DEFAULTS TO EFFORT medium WHERE OPUS 5 DEFAULTED TO high. This entry
should declare `effort: high`, and `claude_builder` `max_iterations: 100`
(3 of 8 builder runs exhausted the 50-call limit) — both wait on
lagrange-framework REQ-203: `configureBackends` rejects a key it does not
declare, so naming either today would stop the host starting.
